q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Gazette of India is published in both Hindi and English.
2. The passenger tickets issued by the Indian Railways are printed in Hindi and English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The headquarters of the World Hindi Secretariat (Vishwa Hindi Sachivalaya) is located in Mauritius.
2. World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January every year, was observed for the first time in the year 2006.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the first Indian leader to address the United Nations General Assembly in Hindi.
2. The United Nations has six official languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011:
1. The number of mother tongues returned in the raw returns of the Census was 19,569.
2. Among the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, Sanskrit has the smallest number of speakers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Bihar was the first province in India to adopt Hindi in the Devanagari script in place of Persian for court work, in the year 1881.
2. Uttar Pradesh was the first State to adopt Hindi as its official language, by an Act passed in the year 1951.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Nagari Pracharini Sabha, founded in the year 1893 for the promotion of the Devanagari script, was established at Varanasi.
2. The Dakshin Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha was founded by Mahatma Gandhi at Madras in the year 1918.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of Bangladesh is Bengali.
2. The official language of Pakistan is Urdu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. In the year 2019, Hindi was included as one of the official languages of the courts of Abu Dhabi.
2. Arabic became one of the official languages of the United Nations in the year 1973.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
2. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, the reports of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities are caused to be laid before each House of Parliament, and sent to the Governments of the States concerned, by the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The standard of the Prabodh course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the Hindi standard of the primary (Class V) level.
2. The standard of the Praveen course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the Hindi standard of the middle (Class VIII) level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Quarterly Progress Report from the Annual Assessment Report on the progressive use of Hindi?

options.A: The Quarterly Progress Report is prepared by the Department of Official Language and laid before Parliament, while the Annual Assessment Report is sent by an office to its controlling office
options.B: The Quarterly Progress Report is sent by a Central Government office to its controlling office or administrative Ministry/Department, while the Annual Assessment Report is prepared by the Department of Official Language and laid before both Houses of Parliament
options.C: Both reports are prepared by the Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.D: Both reports are sent by a Central Government office directly to the President

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes a Town Official Language Implementation Committee from the Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office?

options.A: The Town Committee is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language, while the office Committee is chaired by the District Magistrate
options.B: The Town Committee meets every quarter, while the office Committee meets twice a year
options.C: The Town Committee is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer in the town and meets twice a year, while the office Committee is chaired by the head of the office and meets every quarter
options.D: Both Committees are chaired by the head of the office and meet every quarter

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes 'personal pay' from a 'lumpsum award' under the incentive schemes relating to the Hindi examinations?

options.A: Personal pay is admissible only on retirement, while a lumpsum award is admissible during service
options.B: Personal pay is admissible to an employee who passes the examination through his own efforts without training, while a lumpsum award is equal to one increment for 12 months
options.C: Personal pay is a cash prize for original noting in Hindi, while a lumpsum award is given for Hindi typing only
options.D: Personal pay equal to one increment is admissible for a period of 12 months on passing the prescribed Hindi examination, while a lumpsum award is admissible to an employee who passes the examination through his own efforts (self-study), without undergoing the prescribed training

q: Two States agree between themselves that Hindi shall be the language for communication between them. Under the proviso to Article 346 of the Constitution, the official language for communication between those States will be:

options.C: The official language of the first State
options.D: The official language of the second State

q: A member of Parliament finds that he is unable to express himself adequately in Hindi or English and wishes to address the House in his mother tongue. Under Article 120 of the Constitution, he may do so with the permission of:

options.B: The presiding officer of the House (the Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be)

q: The Legislature of a State has prescribed a language other than English for use in Bills introduced in that Legislature. A translation of a Bill in English is published under the authority of the Governor in the Official Gazette of the State. Under Article 348(3) of the Constitution, that translation shall be deemed to be:

options.A: A mere unofficial summary of the Bill
options.C: The authoritative text thereof in the English language
options.D: A draft requiring the approval of Parliament

q: In a State where the use of Hindi for judgments, decrees or orders of the High Court has been authorised under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a judgment is delivered in Hindi. Under that Section, the judgment must be accompanied by:

options.A: A summary of the judgment in the regional language
options.B: A Hindi translation of the English text
options.C: A certificate of the Registrar of the High Court
options.D: A translation thereof in the English language issued under the authority of the High Court

q: An employee of a Central Government office (not being an office notified under Rule 10(4)) possesses working knowledge of Hindi but prefers to do his noting and drafting in English. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is that he:

options.A: May make noting and drafting in Hindi or in English, as he may choose
options.B: Must do all noting and drafting in Hindi only
options.C: Must obtain the permission of the head of the office for every noting in English
options.D: Must furnish a Hindi translation of every noting made in English

q: A Central Government office, citing urgency of the file, issues its general orders in English only. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that general orders are required to be issued:

options.A: In English only, when the matter is urgent
options.D: In the regional language of the State where the office is located

q: A citizen submits a representation for the redress of his grievance to a Central Government office in Bengali, a language used in his State. The office proposes to return it on the ground that representations are entertained only in Hindi or English. Under Article 350 of the Constitution, the correct position is that every person is entitled to submit such a representation in:

options.C: Any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be
options.D: The official language of the Union only

q: A Ministry of the Central Government issues a communication to its attached office situated in Region 'A'. The dealing officer insists that every such communication must, without exception, be issued in Hindi alone. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Ministry or Department to its attached and subordinate offices situated in Region 'A' shall be in Hindi:

options.A: Only when the attached office demands it
options.C: In every case, without any exception
options.D: In such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time

q: A Central Government office releases an advertisement only in the regional language newspaper of the area. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, the advertisement should have been released:

options.A: In Hindi and English (bilingual), i.e., in both Hindi and English newspapers
options.B: In the regional language newspaper only, as it is meant for the local public
options.C: In Hindi newspapers only during Hindi Pakhwada
options.D: In English newspapers only, as advertisements are meant for the educated public

q: Which of the following pairs relating to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is NOT correctly matched?

options.A: Sanskrit — Included in the Eighth Schedule as originally enacted
options.B: Sindhi — Added to the Eighth Schedule in the year 1967
options.C: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali — Added to the Eighth Schedule in the year 1992
options.D: English — Included in the Eighth Schedule as originally enacted

q:
Match the States with the Region in which they are placed under the Official Language Rules, 1976:
1. Maharashtra, 2. Kerala, 3. Assam, 4. Goa
(a) Region 'A', (b) Region 'B', (c) Region 'C', (d) Region 'C'
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the events relating to the Official Language?

options.A: Official Language Rules — First World Hindi Conference — Central Hindi Training Institute — First observance of World Hindi Day
options.B: First World Hindi Conference — Official Language Rules — Central Hindi Training Institute — First observance of World Hindi Day
options.C: Central Hindi Training Institute — First World Hindi Conference — Official Language Rules — First observance of World Hindi Day
options.D: First observance of World Hindi Day — Central Hindi Training Institute — Official Language Rules — First World Hindi Conference

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English accounting term "Cash Book" is:
The standard Hindi equivalent of the English accounting term "Journal" is:
The standard Hindi equivalent of the English accounting term "Debit" is:
The standard Hindi equivalent of the English accounting term "Credit" is:
The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Office" is:

Match the Articles of the Constitution with their subject matter:
1. Article 344, 2. Article 346, 3. Article 349, 4. Article 350B
(a) Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, (b) Language for communication between the Union and a State, or between one State and another, (c) Commission and Committee of Parliament on Official Language, (d) Special procedure in respect of Bills relating to the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts

Match the Sections of the Official Languages Act, 1963 with their subject matter:
1. Section 3, 2. Section 4, 3. Section 6, 4. Section 8
(a) Power of the Central Government to make rules, (b) Committee of Parliament on Official Language, (c) Authoritative text in Hindi of Acts of a State Legislature passed in a language other than Hindi, (d) Continued use of English and issue of specified documents in both Hindi and English

Match the States/Union Territories with the Region in which they are placed under the Official Language Rules, 1976:
1. Haryana, 2. Punjab, 3. Karnataka, 4. Tamil Nadu
(a) Region 'A', (b) Region 'B', (c) Region 'C', (d) Region 'C'

Match the courses of the Hindi Teaching Scheme with their description:
1. Prabodh, 2. Praveen, 3. Pragya, 4. Parangat
(a) The next course to be undergone after passing Prabodh, (b) The course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi, (c) The first prescribed course, (d) The final prescribed course for clerical (ministerial) staff

Match the languages with the scripts with which they are associated:
1. Maithili, 2. Bhojpuri, 3. Assamese, 4. Lepcha
(a) Rong script, (b) Tirhuta (Mithilakshar) script, (c) Kaithi script, (d) Eastern Nagari (Bengali-Assamese) script

Match the celebrated Hindi works with their authors:
1. Prem Sagar, 2. Jhootha Sach, 3. Andha Yug, 4. Hindi Sahitya ka Itihas
(a) Yashpal, (b) Lallu Lal, (c) Acharya Ramchandra Shukla, (d) Dharamvir Bharati

Match the committees relating to the Official Language with the person who chairs them:
1. Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee), 2. Central Official Language Implementation Committee, 3. Town Official Language Implementation Committee, 4. Hindi Salahakar Samiti of a Union Ministry
(a) The Minister in charge of the Ministry concerned, (b) The Prime Minister, (c) The Secretary, Department of Official Language, (d) The senior-most Central Government officer in the town

Match the English administrative terms with their standard Hindi equivalents:
1. Memorandum, 2. Circular, 3. Reminder, 4. Allowance
(a) Bhatta, (b) Gyapan, (c) Anusmarak, (d) Paripatra

Match the English administrative terms with their standard Hindi equivalents:
1. Balance Sheet, 2. Ledger, 3. Audit, 4. Advance
(a) Khata Bahi, (b) Agrim, (c) Tulan Patra, (d) Lekha Pariksha

Match the items of the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi with the target fixed for them:
1. Correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A', 2. Correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B', 3. Correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C', 4. Noting on files in Hindi
(a) 55 per cent, (b) 30 per cent, (c) 100 per cent, (d) 90 per cent

Consider the following statements:
1. The authoritative text of the Constitution of India in the Hindi language is published under the authority of the President in accordance with Article 394A, inserted by the Constitution (58th Amendment) Act, 1987.
2. The First World Hindi Conference, held at Nagpur, was inaugurated by Smt. Indira Gandhi, the then Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Gazette of India is published in both Hindi and English.
2. 'Trains at a Glance', the All India Railway Time Table published by the Indian Railways, is published in Hindi and English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The websites of Central Government offices are required to be maintained in Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form.
2. For Hindi (Devanagari) typing on computers in Central Government offices, the keyboard layout adopted as the standard is known as InScript.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya for employees who cannot attend regular classes are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.
2. In-service Hindi training imparted to an employee during office hours is free of cost and the training period is treated as on duty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Personal pay equal to one increment is admissible to an employee for a period of 12 months on passing the prescribed Hindi examination.
2. Under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi, an employee becomes eligible for consideration for a cash award on doing noting and drafting in Hindi of at least 10,000 words in a year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. To ensure compliance with Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, certain points in a Central Government office, such as the despatch section, are designated as 'Check Points'.
2. The Annual Assessment Report on the implementation of the Annual Programme is prepared by the Department of Official Language and is laid before both Houses of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011:
1. The number of mother tongues returned in the raw returns of the Census was 19,569.
2. Hindi is the mother tongue of about 43.6 per cent of the population of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The United Nations has six official languages.
2. Arabic became one of the official languages of the United Nations in the year 1973.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. In the year 2019, Hindi was included as one of the official languages of the courts of Abu Dhabi.
2. Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the first Indian leader to address the United Nations General Assembly in Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Bihar was the first province in India to adopt Hindi in the Devanagari script in place of Persian for court work, in the year 1881.
2. The Nagari Pracharini Sabha, founded in the year 1893 for the promotion of the Devanagari script, was established at Varanasi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Uttar Pradesh was the first State to adopt Hindi as its official language, by an Act passed in the year 1951.
2. The Dakshin Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha was founded by Mahatma Gandhi at Madras in the year 1918.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of Bangladesh is Bengali.
2. The headquarters of the World Hindi Secretariat (Vishwa Hindi Sachivalaya) is located in Mauritius.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court has been authorised by the Governor with the previous consent of the President in the State of Bihar.
2. The use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court has been authorised by the Governor with the previous consent of the President in the State of West Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. 'Ashtadhyayi', the celebrated treatise on Sanskrit grammar, was composed by Panini.
2. The inscriptions (edicts) of Emperor Ashoka are mostly written in the Prakrit language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

A Central Government office situated in Region 'A' sends an ordinary communication to another Central Government office situated in Region 'A', the communication not being one between a Ministry or Department and its attached or subordinate office. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication shall be in:

options.C: The regional language of the State
options.D: Hindi and the regional language, in equal proportion

q: At a check point in a Central Government office, a notification covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 is presented for despatch in English only. The correct course of action is:

options.A: To despatch it in English, urgency of issue being a valid ground
options.B: To despatch it in English and send the Hindi version a week later
options.C: Not to let the document leave the office unless it is issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: To translate it into Hindi at the check point and despatch the Hindi version alone

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 65 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 89 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi typewriting examination
options.C: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the stenography examination being 88 per cent or more marks

q: An employee aged 46 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He must undergo the training, as in-service Hindi training is compulsory for every employee
options.B: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He must undergo the training on payment of the prescribed fee

q: In a Central Government office, 82 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi and the office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976. An employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi is directed to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification. The direction is:

options.A: Not in order, as noting and drafting can never be required to be done in Hindi
options.B: In order only during Hindi Pakhwada
options.D: In order only with the written consent of the employee

q: A Central Government office sends an ordinary communication in English to a State Government office located in Region 'C'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication:

options.A: Is in order, communications to offices in Region 'C' being ordinarily issued in English
options.B: Must be returned by the receiving office for want of Hindi
options.C: Must be accompanied by its Hindi translation in every case
options.D: Is prohibited, English being barred for communication with Region 'C'

q: A letter in Hindi is received in a Central Government office located in Region 'B'. The dealing assistant proposes to reply in English, on the ground that the office is located in a non-Hindi speaking region. The correct position under the Official Language Rules is:

options.A: The reply may be sent in English, Region 'B' being exempt from Hindi correspondence
options.B: The reply must be sent in the regional language of the State
options.C: The reply may be sent in either language at the discretion of the dealing assistant
options.D: The letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, the target for such replies being 100 per cent

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 4 from Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Both the Sections deal only with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.B: Section 4 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 8 vests the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act in the Central Government
options.C: Section 4 vests the rule-making power in the Central Government, while Section 8 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.D: Both the Sections deal only with the rule-making power of the Central Government

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Central Hindi Directorate from the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi), Agra?

options.A: The Central Hindi Directorate conducts the correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, while the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan is engaged in teaching Hindi to non-Hindi speaking Indian and foreign learners, training of Hindi teachers and research in Hindi
options.B: The Central Hindi Directorate teaches Hindi to foreign learners, while the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan conducts the correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya
options.C: Both the bodies only conduct the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations
options.D: Both the bodies are engaged only in the translation of codes and manuals

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Prabodh from Parangat under the Hindi Teaching Scheme?

options.A: Both are the first course prescribed for employees who do not possess any knowledge of Hindi
options.B: Prabodh is the course prescribed beyond Pragya, while Parangat is the first prescribed course
options.C: Parangat is the first prescribed course, while Prabodh is the final prescribed course for clerical staff
options.D: Prabodh is the first prescribed course, while Parangat is the course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Hindi Diwas from Hindi Pakhwada?

options.A: Both are observed on 10th January every year
options.B: Hindi Diwas is a fortnight-long observance, while Hindi Pakhwada is observed on a single day
options.C: Hindi Diwas is observed on 14th September, marking the adoption of Hindi as the Official Language in 1949, while Hindi Pakhwada is the fortnight from 14th September to 28th September observed in Central Government offices for promoting the use of Hindi
options.D: Hindi Diwas is observed only abroad, while Hindi Pakhwada is observed only in Region 'A'

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Quarterly Progress Report from the questionnaire (Prashnavali) relating to the Official Language?

options.A: The Quarterly Progress Report is filled in by an office only when the Committee of Parliament visits it, while the questionnaire is sent by the office to its controlling office every quarter
options.B: The Quarterly Progress Report is sent periodically by a Central Government office to its controlling office or administrative Ministry/Department, while the questionnaire is filled in by the office to furnish detailed information about implementation to the Committee of Parliament on Official Language before its inspection visit
options.C: Both are prepared by the Department of Official Language and laid before Parliament
options.D: Both are submitted by a Central Government office directly to the President

q: Which of the following statements about the institutions relating to the Official Language is FALSE?

options.A: The Central Hindi Directorate was established in the year 1960
options.B: The Central Translation Bureau was set up in the year 1971
options.C: The Department of Official Language was set up in the year 1975
options.D: The Central Hindi Training Institute was established in the year 1960

q: Which of the following statements about the courses under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is FALSE?

options.A: Parangat is the first course prescribed for employees who do not possess any knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The standard of the Prabodh course corresponds broadly to the primary (Class V) level
options.C: The standard of the Praveen course corresponds broadly to the middle (Class VIII) level
options.D: The standard of the Pragya course corresponds broadly to the Matriculation (Class X) level

q: Which of the following statements about the Rajbhasha awards is FALSE?

options.A: The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.B: The Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division in Regions 'A' and 'B'
options.C: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.D: The Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division in Region 'C'

q: Which of the following statements about the targets under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi is FALSE?

options.A: The target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A' is 100 per cent
options.B: The target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' is 90 per cent
options.C: The target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' is 90 per cent
options.D: The target fixed for noting on files in Hindi is 30 per cent

q: Which of the following pairs of a Constitution Amendment Act and the addition of a language to the Eighth Schedule is NOT correctly matched?

options.A: Constitution (21st Amendment) Act — Sindhi added to the Eighth Schedule
options.B: Constitution (71st Amendment) Act — Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali added to the Eighth Schedule
options.C: Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act — Dogri added to the Eighth Schedule
options.D: Constitution (96th Amendment) Act — Sindhi added to the Eighth Schedule

q: Which of the following pairs of an Article of the Constitution and its subject matter is NOT correctly matched?

options.A: Article 349 — Directive for the development of the Hindi language
options.B: Article 347 — Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State, on a direction of the President
options.C: Article 350A — Facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
options.D: Article 350B — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities

q: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of these events: the first celebration of Hindi Diwas, the appointment of the first Official Language Commission, the Presidential Order of 1960 and the enactment of the Official Languages Act?

options.A: First Official Language Commission — First celebration of Hindi Diwas — Official Languages Act — Presidential Order
options.B: First celebration of Hindi Diwas — Presidential Order — First Official Language Commission — Official Languages Act
options.C: First celebration of Hindi Diwas — First Official Language Commission — Presidential Order — Official Languages Act
options.D: Official Languages Act — First celebration of Hindi Diwas — First Official Language Commission — Presidential Order

q: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of these developments: the Official Languages Act, the Official Language Resolution, the Official Language Rules and the establishment of the Central Hindi Training Institute?

options.A: Official Language Rules — Official Languages Act — Official Language Resolution — Central Hindi Training Institute
options.B: Official Languages Act — Official Language Resolution — Official Language Rules — Central Hindi Training Institute
options.C: Official Languages Act — Official Language Rules — Official Language Resolution — Central Hindi Training Institute
options.D: Official Language Resolution — Official Languages Act — Central Hindi Training Institute — Official Language Rules

q:
Match the institutions relating to the Official Language with the year of their establishment:
1. Sahitya Akademi, 2. Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysuru, 3. Central Hindi Training Institute, 4. Department of Official Language
(a) 1969, (b) 1985, (c) 1954, (d) 1975

Match the events relating to the Official Language with the year in which they took place:
1. Submission of the report of the first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission) to the President, 2. Issue of the Presidential Order on official language, 3. Presidential assent to the Official Languages Act, 4. Adoption of the Official Language Resolution by Parliament
(a) 1960, (b) 1968, (c) 1956, (d) 1963

Match the States with the Region in which they are placed under the Official Language Rules, 1976:
1. Rajasthan, 2. Gujarat, 3. Odisha, 4. Sikkim
(a) Region 'A', (b) Region 'B', (c) Region 'C', (d) Region 'C'

Match the States/Union Territories with the Region in which they are placed under the Official Language Rules, 1976:
1. Delhi, 2. Chandigarh, 3. Andhra Pradesh, 4. Manipur
(a) Region 'B', (b) Region 'C', (c) Region 'A', (d) Region 'C'

Match the States with their official languages:
1. Maharashtra, 2. Gujarat, 3. Kerala, 4. Tamil Nadu
(a) Gujarati, (b) Tamil, (c) Marathi, (d) Malayalam

Match the languages with the script in which they were traditionally written:
1. Dogri, 2. Maithili, 3. Marathi, 4. Kashmiri
(a) Modi script, (b) Sharada script, (c) Takri script, (d) Tirhuta (Mithilakshar) script

Match the languages with the year in which they were accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India:
1. Tamil, 2. Sanskrit, 3. Malayalam, 4. Marathi
(a) 2013, (b) 2005, (c) 2024, (d) 2004

Match the World Hindi Conferences with the places where they were held:
1. Fourth World Hindi Conference, 2. Eighth World Hindi Conference, 3. Ninth World Hindi Conference, 4. Twelfth World Hindi Conference
(a) New York, (b) Nadi (Fiji), (c) Port Louis (Mauritius), (d) Johannesburg (South Africa)

Match the celebrated Hindi works with their authors:
1. Saket, 2. Raag Darbari, 3. Tamas, 4. Chitralekha
(a) Bhisham Sahni, (b) Maithili Sharan Gupt, (c) Bhagwati Charan Verma, (d) Shrilal Shukla

Match the celebrated Hindi works with their authors:
1. Vinay Patrika, 2. Sursagar, 3. Chandrakanta, 4. Maila Anchal
(a) Surdas, (b) Phanishwar Nath Renu, (c) Goswami Tulsidas, (d) Devaki Nandan Khatri

Match the English administrative terms with their standard Hindi equivalents:
1. Memorandum, 2. Notification, 3. Resolution, 4. Order
